title: Graph-supported comparison for semilinear sum extension
statement:
Let $e:U\to T$ be a separated etale morphism of finite type of schemes, and choose a compactification $e=pj$ with $j:U\hookrightarrow\overline U$ quasi-compact open and $p:\overline U\to T$ proper. Let $R_1\leftarrow R_2\leftarrow\cdots$ be any inverse sequence of commutative rings. For each scheme use its small pro-etale site and constant ring sheaves $(R_n)$, and write $\mathscr S_Z$ for the category of strict semilinear module sections $M_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}_{n+1,n}M_n$ as in [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Let $e_{\Sigma!,\bullet}$ be levelwise sheafification of the direct-sum presheaf
$$V\longmapsto\bigoplus_{t:V\to U\,/T}M_n(V,t)$$
of [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf]. Its derived functor is the exact degreewise functor, denoted $De_{\Sigma!,\bullet}$.

The graph $\Gamma_t:V\to\overline U\times_TV$ of each lift $t$ is an open and closed immersion. The section equal to $m\in M_n(V,t)$ on this graph and zero on its complement is a section of $j_!M_n$ on $\overline U\times_TV$. The sum of these maps on the presheaf summands induces a module-sheaf map $e_{\Sigma!,\bullet}M\to p_{*,\bullet}j_{!,\bullet}M$, natural in $M$ and compatible with all pro-etale restrictions and semilinear transitions. Using the simultaneous derived operations and their comparison maps of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections], the degreewise graph map followed by the derived direct-image comparison gives a natural transformation
$$\theta:De_{\Sigma!,\bullet}\longrightarrow Rp_{*,\bullet}j_{!,\bullet}$$
in the ordinary derived categories of sections. Its evaluation at $n$ is the analogous graph natural transformation of functors from $D(U_{\mathrm{proet}},R_n)$ to $D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},R_n)$. If $T,U,\overline U$ are separated of finite type over a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$, $R_n$ is a finite ring killed by a power of a prime $\ell\ne p$, and the input is the etale pullback $\nu_U^*L$ of a bounded constructible finite-Tor complex, then $\theta_n$ equals the inverse of the finite etale sum-extension normalization of [lem-pur-etale-support-map-compatibility] transported via the specified compact-support comparison of [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility]. Here the sum-extension site comparison $\nu_T^*e_{\Sigma!}^{\mathrm{et}}\simeq e_{\Sigma!}^{\mathrm{proet}}\nu_U^*$ is the adjunction-preserving one obtained from the localized-site direct-image identification [lem-weil-pbc-localize-ringed-site-morphism]. This assertion specifies the graph map and its finite evaluation, without asserting it is an isomorphism on arbitrary inputs.

proof.text: For a pro-etale test object V→T and a lift t:V→U, base change of the separated etale map e makes U×_T V→V separated etale. Its graph Γ_t is a section, hence an open and closed immersion by the etale-section lemma. The open immersion U×_T V→\overline U×_T V carries this graph to an open subscheme, while the same graph is closed in the latter product because it is a section of the separated base change of the proper morphism p. The graph therefore has an open-and-closed decomposition in the open part and a closed image in the compactification, exactly the geometry used for extension by zero. In particular the graph is clopen in the whole compactified product, since its open immersion is the composite of the graph open immersion with the base-changed open immersion.

proof.text: Put $\overline U_V=\overline U\times_TV$. Since Step 1 makes $\Gamma_t$ clopen in $\overline U_V$, use the disjoint open cover $\overline U_V=\Gamma_t\amalg(\overline U_V\setminus\Gamma_t)$ to glue $m\in M_n(V,t)$ and zero as sections of $j_!M_n$. On the graph, which lies in $U\times_TV$, open extension restricts to $M_n$; hence the gluing exists, is unique and is linear. Pullback of this cover along $V'\to V$ is the graph/complement cover for $t|_{V'}$, so uniqueness proves compatibility with restrictions. Finite sums of these maps define a presheaf-module map from [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf] to $p_*j_!M_n$. Sheafification and [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact] give the module-sheaf map. For a semilinear transition, both composites have the transitioned value on the same graph and zero on the complement; uniqueness proves the transition identity, without any flatness assumption on the ring maps.

proof.text: The maps of Step 2 are natural in the coefficient sheaf because a module morphism commutes with restriction to the graph and to its complement. Apply the simultaneous section models for exact levelwise operations and their adjunction-mate comparisons from [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. The underived map sheafifies and then derives to a natural transformation θ:De_{Σ!,bullet}→Rp_{*,bullet}j_{!,bullet}. No inverse or isomorphism assertion is used in this construction.

proof.text: The evaluation clause of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections] applies to any strict inverse ring system, with no restriction to $\mathcal O_E/\ell^n$. Evaluation preserves the exact sum extension, open extension, derived direct image, the sheaf map of Step 2, and the specified adjunction comparisons used in Step 3. Thus evaluation of $\theta$ is precisely the analogous graph natural transformation $\theta_n:D(U_{\mathrm{proet}},R_n)\to D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},R_n)$ formed by the degreewise map followed by the derived direct-image comparison. No compact-support evaluation theorem for a special coefficient tower is needed.

proof.text:
For the finite comparison fix a finite ring $A=R_n$. By [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization], $U_{\mathrm{proet}}$ is the ringed slice $T_{\mathrm{proet}}/U$, with the same constant $A$-sheaf. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localize-ringed-site-morphism] to the etale/pro-etale comparison and the object $U$. Its direct-image comparison is the identity on etale test objects, with the restricted ring action. Both $
u_T^*e_{\Sigma!}^{\mathrm{et}}$ and $e_{\Sigma!}^{\mathrm{proet}}
u_U^*$ are left adjoint to the resulting common right adjoint $
u_{U,*}e_{\mathrm{proet}}^*=e_{\mathrm{et}}^*
u_{T,*}$, using the exact slice sum-extension adjunction. The unique comparison preserving these adjunctions is
$$\sigma:
u_T^*e_{\Sigma!}^{\mathrm{et}}\xrightarrow{\sim}e_{\Sigma!}^{\mathrm{proet}}
u_U^*.$$
On an etale test object $W	o T$ it sends the image of a presheaf generator $(t,m)$ to the image of $(t,\eta_M(m))$: indeed the two adjunction units put $m$ in the same lift summand, and the localized direct-image identity changes neither $W$ nor $t$. This is an assertion about generators before sheafification, not an objectwise direct-sum formula for sheaf sections.

proof.text:
Now assume the finite clause of the item: $k$ is any field of characteristic $p>0$, $A$ is finite of $\ell$-power exponent with $\ell\ne p$, the schemes are separated finite type over $k$, and $L$ is bounded constructible finite-Tor. The schemes are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] ($\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian since its only ideals are $0,k$), and $p$ is qcqs because it is proper. Choose a bounded representative $K$ of $L$ and put $P=j_!^{\mathrm{et}}K$ in Step 7. Apply $Q$ to Step 6 degreewise, then the pro-etale comparison $\gamma$. Naturality of $\gamma$ for $o_K$, followed by Step 7, gives explicitly
$$\begin{aligned}
\theta_n(\nu_U^*L)\sigma_L
&=\gamma^{\mathrm{proet}}Q(G^{\mathrm{proet}}_{\nu_U^*K})\sigma_K\\
&=Rp_*^{\mathrm{proet}}(o_K)\gamma^{\mathrm{proet}}_{\nu^*P}Q(d_{p,P})\nu_T^*Q(G^{\mathrm{et}}_K)\\
&=Rp_*^{\mathrm{proet}}(o_K)b_{p,QP}\nu_T^*(\gamma_P^{\mathrm{et}}Q(G^{\mathrm{et}}_K))\\
&=c_{e,A}^c(L)\nu_T^*((c_e^{c,\mathrm{et}}(L))^{-1}).
\end{aligned}$$
Here $c_e^{c,\mathrm{et}}$ is the sum-extension normalization of [lem-pur-etale-support-map-compatibility], whose inverse is exactly $\gamma^{\mathrm{et}}Q(G^{\mathrm{et}})$; $c_{e,A}^c=Rp_*^{\mathrm{proet}}(o)b_p$ is precisely the compact-support site comparison defined in [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility]. Thus the displayed equation proves the requested finite normalization with the specified $\sigma$, not just existence of an isomorphism. These are identities of the natural transformations on representatives, so [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] makes them equal as derived natural transformations; no finite-field hypothesis on $k$ or coefficient-change assertion is used.
